name: Adina
title: Warrior from the tribe of Reuben among David's mighty men
summary: Adina, son of Shiza the Reubenite, was a prominent warrior in King David's service. He is listed in the expanded roster of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles, among the names that supplement the well-known circle of thirty heroes. According to the text, Adina led thirty men from the tribe of Reuben, pointing to a significant military position within David's army structure. His presence in this list is historically interesting because the tribe of Reuben settled east of the Jordan, in Transjordan. That a warrior from there held a prominent place in David's military elite testifies that the king's power base and network of loyalty included tribes on both sides of the Jordan River.

keyEvents.title: Listed among David's mighty men
keyEvents.description: Adina, son of Shiza the Reubenite, is mentioned in the list of David's mighty warriors in 1 Chronicles. He is highlighted as one of the names beyond the original circle of thirty heroes, holding a leading position over thirty men from the tribe of Reuben. This shows his significance in David's military organization and that royal power had broad support from tribes on both sides of the Jordan.

versions.summary: Adina, son of Shiza from the tribe of Reuben, was one of King David's mighty warriors. He is mentioned among the thirty heroes who served David, and he was leader over thirty men from the tribe of Reuben. His mention is found in 1 Chronicles.
versions.title: One of David's mighty warriors
versions.reason: [major] 1 Chr 11:10-12 concerns the three most powerful heroes (Jashobeam, Eleazar), not Adina specifically. Adina is first mentioned in verse 42. This event should either be removed or the references corrected.; [major] 1 Chr 12:37-38 concerns the tribes that gathered to make David king in Hebron, not Adina specifically. This is a general reference about the tribe of Reuben but does not directly link to Adina.; [minor] The events "Listed among David's heroes" and "Leader over thirty from the tribe of Reuben" both refer to exactly the same verse (1 Chr 11:42) and could usefully be combined into one event to avoid repetition.; [minor] The phrasing "among the thirty heroes" can be misleading. The text in 1 Chr 11:42 states that he was "beyond the thirty" (that is, in addition to the thirty), and that he had thirty with him. Adina was thus not part of the original thirty but is mentioned beyond this group.; [minor] The title is generic. A more precise title could mention his connection to the tribe of Reuben to distinguish him from other of David's warriors.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. The name Adina, his tribal affiliation, and the context surrounding the list in 1 Chr 11 deserve historical and linguistic notes.

versions.summary: Adina, son of Shiza, was a Reubenite who served among King David's mighty warriors. He is mentioned in the list of David's heroes in 1 Chronicles, where he is noted beyond the original thirty heroes. Adina held a leading position with thirty men under him from the tribe of Reuben, testifying to his military authority. His presence among David's closest fighters shows that David's support extended also to the tribes east of the Jordan.
versions.title: Warrior from the tribe of Reuben among David's mighty men
versions.reason: [minor] The second key event ('Representative of the tribes east of the Jordan') is actually a theological/historical interpretation of the same verse (1 Chr 11:42) and not an independent event. It largely repeats information from the first event. It may be considered to merge them or rephrase the second one to have a clearer separate focus.; [minor] The phrasing 'beyond the original thirty mighty men' is somewhat unclear. The Hebrew text in 1 Chr 11:42 can be interpreted as Adina being 'beyond the thirty' (that is, in addition to the thirty), but it should be formulated more clearly to avoid misunderstandings.; [minor] The role 'leader' can be clarified to 'military leader' to provide more specificity regarding his function as commander over thirty warriors from the tribe of Reuben.

versions.summary:
Adina, son of Shiza the Reubenite, was one of King David's prominent warriors.  
He is listed in the expanded roster of David’s mighty men in 1 Chronicles, among the names added to the thirty most famous heroes.  
Adina led a group of thirty men from the tribe of Reuben, testifying to his military authority and rank.  
As a representative of a tribe with territory east of the Jordan, his place among David’s warrior heroes illustrates that the king’s power base extended broadly across Israel’s tribes, including those in Transjordan.
versions.title: Warrior from the tribe of Reuben among David's mighty men
versions.reason: [minor] The summary is well formulated and theologically correct. There is some overlap between sentences three and four (both concern the tribe's broad representation). It could be tightened slightly to avoid repetition, but this is a marginal improvement.; [minor] The role 'military leader' is reasonable given that the text describes him as leading thirty men, but it should be clarified that this is a minor leadership position (leader of a tribal contingent), not a supreme commander. The roles 'tribal leader' or 'officer' could have been considered, but 'military leader' is acceptable.; [minor] Footnote 3 mentions '1 Chronicles 11' and '2 Samuel 23' as specific references, which is good. However, the formulation 'the Chronicler' as a designation for the author is an academic convention that is acceptable.

footnotes.text: The name Adina (Hebrew: עֲדִינָא) probably means 'delicate' or 'pleasant'. It is remarkable that a warrior bears such a gentle name, which may indicate that the name was given at birth without reference to his later career.

The tribe of Reuben had its territory east of the Jordan (Transjordan), in the area that today corresponds to parts of northern Jordan. That a Reubenite was among David's warrior heroes shows that David's support extended also to the tribes on the east side of the Jordan, underscoring his legitimacy as king over all Israel.

The list of David's heroes in 1 Chronicles 11 expands upon the corresponding list in 2 Samuel 23. Adina and several other names (verses 41–47) are found only in the version of the books of Chronicles, suggesting that the author had access to additional sources about David's military organization.

That Adina is described as leader over thirty men from the tribe of Reuben may reflect a military organization based on tribal affiliation in David's army. This structure has parallels in the tribe-based military system known from other Old Testament texts, and testifies to a decentralized military organization.

The textual tradition surrounding 1 Chron. 11:42 varies somewhat. Some manuscripts and translations have different readings regarding the description of Adina's role, which has given rise to various interpretations as to whether he led thirty men or was himself 'over the thirty' in rank.

The expanded names in 1 Chron. 11:41–47 are missing from the parallel list in 2 Sam. 23. Some scholars have suggested that these names may come from a separate source linked to David's time in Ziklag or during the early years of his kingdom, when he built alliances with tribes on both sides of the Jordan.
